app.hr_employee.title: Employee Self-Service
app.hr_employee.description: View your schedule, leave, pay components, loans, payslips, and profile
app.hr_employee.header_description: Your schedule, leave, pay components, loans, payslips, and employment history in one place.
app.hr_employee.no_active_employment: No active employment on your record
app.hr_employee.no_active_employment_des: Time, leave, claims, loans, and payslips are all recorded against an employment, so there is nothing to show or submit until HR opens one for you. This is missing employment data, not a restriction on your access — ask HR to add your employment.
app.hr_employee.choose_employment: Choose the employment you are working in
app.hr_employee.choose_employment_descri: Your requests, time, loans, and payslips will be scoped to this employment.
app.hr_employee.search_employment: Search by company or employee number…
app.hr_employee.my_time_description: Raw clock events keyed by employment and explicit local work date.
app.hr_employee.my_leave_description: Submit leave and track the approved request that directly updates payroll and balance.
app.hr_employee.my_components_descriptio: Claims, allowances, arrears, and loan instalments, with why each entry exists.
app.hr_employee.my_loans_description: Loans still being repaid today: the agreed principal and the instalments it is being repaid by. Drop the effective-range filter for settled ones.
app.hr_employee.my_payslips_description: Review payroll results and a safe explanation of every line.
app.hr_controller.title: HR Controller

app.leave.title: Leave
app.leave.description: Review leave events and the leave types that entitle them
app.leave.header_description: Decide time-off requests against the leave type's layered entitlement matrix — scoped to one legal entity.

app.leave.empty_types: Select a legal entity to manage its leave types.
app.leave.leave_activity_description: {count} time-off requests. Balances are derived directly from approved leave events at read time — there is no duplicate ledger, stored balance, or accrual job.
app.leave.leave_decisions_note: Counts use the leave period start date. Approval speed is shown only when completed workflow history exists; imported records do not invent a duration.
app.leave.chart_description: Application volume across the five completed calendar years, with a least-squares regression line.
app.loans.title: Loans
app.loans.description: Review staff loans, salary advances, and overpayment recoveries with their derived outstanding balance
app.loans.header_description: Repayment agreements deduct a principal over time — scoped to one legal entity. Outstanding is derived from scheduled instalments linked to payslips, never stored separately.
app.loans.empty: Select a legal entity to review its repayment agreements.
app.loans.repayment_agreements_descripti: Outstanding falls when a scheduled entry is linked to a payslip.
app.pay_components.title: Pay components
app.pay_components.description: Review pay-component entries — allowances, claims, arrears, reversals, and loan instalments — and their payroll linkage
app.pay_components.header_description: The company catalogue and the single entry stream money reaches payroll through — scoped to one legal entity. A live entry is one with no open approval; there is no separate requested/approved state.
app.pay_components.empty_overview: Select a legal entity to load claim activity.
app.pay_components.empty_entries: Select a legal entity to review its pay-component entries.
app.pay_components.empty_catalogue: Select a legal entity to manage its pay-component catalogue.
app.pay_components.reimbursement_claims_: {count} claim entries in the ledger. Every other pay component — recurring allowances, one-offs, arrears, reversals, loan instalments — arrives through the same entry stream and is listed under Entries.
app.pay_components.claim_decisions_note: Counts use the claim's incurred date from its origin variant. Approval speed is shown only when completed workflow history exists; imported records do not invent a duration.
app.pay_components.chart_description: Application volume across the five completed calendar years, with a least-squares regression line.

app.payroll.description: Create payroll runs, review payslips, export payments, and audit calculations
app.payroll.header_description: Create a payroll run for a company period, resolve calculation blockers, then review and export employee results — scoped to one legal entity.
app.payroll.empty_overview: Select a legal entity to load payroll cycles.
app.payroll.empty_runs: Select a legal entity to review its payroll runs.
app.payroll.payroll_cycles_description: Pay dates from the company's pay day. Late means the pay date passed without a paid run.
app.payroll.no_open_cycles: No open payroll cycles. Configure a company pay day, or every period is already paid.
app.payroll.payroll_decisions_note: Draft runs and runs held by an approval request count as yet to approve; paid runs count as approved. Speed is the mean completed workflow duration this year.
app.payroll.runs_description: Review payslips against their shared run-level policy snapshot, reconcile totals, export, and pay.
app.payroll.export_bank_files_descriptio: Download bank instructions from stored payslips and the effective employment bank details.
app.payroll.export_bank_files_error: The selected payroll has no bank payments to download.
app.payroll.export_payslip_pdfs_descript: Download employee payslips for any selected run with built results.
app.payroll.export_pdfs_error: The selected payroll runs do not contain built payslips yet.
app.payroll.export_workbook_description: Download the clean Infotech-style salary listing and complete breakdown.
app.people.title: People
app.people.description: Workforce health, and one profile per person carrying their employments, contractual terms and statutory registrations
app.people.header_description: Facts about the human being stay on the person; engagements, dated terms and statutory registrations hang off the employment and are read from that person's profile — scoped to one legal entity.
app.people.empty_overview: Select a legal entity to load workforce metrics.
app.people.empty_trend: Select a legal entity to load the trend chart.
app.people.empty_profiles: Select a legal entity to browse its people.
app.people.workforce_description: Current status is derived from effective employments, not a duplicated employee flag.
app.people.chart_description: Monthly leavers and joiners against average headcount.
app.people.profiles_description: People whose employment is in force today; drop the employment filter for past staff. Open a person for their employments, contractual terms and statutory registrations — everything job-shaped hangs off the engagement, not off the human being.
app.scheduling.title: Scheduling
app.scheduling.description: Plan the monthly roster on a calendar, publish it against the statutory rules, and manage the shifts a day is worked on and the patterns a week is shaped by
app.scheduling.header_description: The month as a calendar — planned shifts and actual attendance in the same cell, with leave, public holidays and the payroll cut-off marked. Publishing a month checks it against the statutory rest rules.
app.scheduling.filters_description: All conditions must match, and they keep whole people.
app.scheduling.import_title: Import planned assignments into the {month} draft from the roster template — one row per person per day, on its "Roster" sheet.
app.scheduling.not_drafted_note: Nothing has been planned for {month} yet, so every day on the board is blank. That is where a month starts, not a fault to fix: create the draft month, then assign or import its days.
app.scheduling.publishing_note: Publishing checks the month against the work pattern: at least one rest day in every week, plus any consecutive-day, daily-hours and between-shift limits the pattern promises. A published month is frozen, so re-open it before correcting a day.
app.scheduling.blocker_no_draft: No roster is drafted for {month}. Create the draft month first, then import into it.
app.scheduling.blocker_published: Roster {month} is published, so its entries are fixed. Re-open the month to import into it.
app.scheduling.toast_publish_not_permitt: Publishing a roster is not permitted for this role.
app.scheduling.toast_publish_failed: The roster could not be published.
app.scheduling.toast_reopen_not_permitte: Re-opening a roster is not permitted for this role.
app.scheduling.toast_reopen_failed: The roster could not be re-opened.
app.scheduling.empty_board: Select a legal entity to load its roster.
app.scheduling.board_load_failed: The {month} board could not be loaded.
app.scheduling.no_matches: No people match the current search or filters.
app.scheduling.empty_shifts: Select a legal entity to manage its shifts.
app.scheduling.shift_intro: A shift definition is one working day: when it starts, when it ends, the unpaid break inside it and whether it runs past midnight. It says nothing about which days of the week are worked — that is a work pattern, which arranges shifts into a week and names one of these as the day it uses.
app.scheduling.empty_patterns: Select a legal entity to manage its work patterns.
app.scheduling.pattern_intro: A work pattern is one week: which weekdays are working, rest and off, which weekday the week starts on, and the scheduling limits a published roster must respect. It carries a default shift for its ordinary days rather than restating one — a rostered pattern derives nothing at all and takes every day from the published roster.
app.scheduling.empty_holidays: Select a legal entity to manage its holidays.
app.settings.title: Statutory profile
app.settings.description: The regime every payroll is calculated against: jurisdictions with the schemes, rates, overtime rules and limits configured inside them, and the companies bound to each
app.settings.header_description: The regime payroll is calculated against, and the companies bound to one. Contribution rates, overtime rules and overtime limits are not catalogues — they are configured inside the jurisdiction that levies them, and rate bands inside the scheme they belong to. The pay catalogue lives under Pay components and per-person registrations under People. Every rule is effective-dated — end-date and insert a successor, never update in place.
app.settings.jurisdictions_description: Open a jurisdiction to configure everything it sets: the statutory schemes it levies (and the rate bands inside each), what overtime is worth, and the ceiling on overtime hours. None of those is a catalogue of its own.
app.settings.companies_description: The legal entities payroll runs for, each bound to the jurisdiction whose regime prices it.
app.time_attendance.title: Time & Attendance
app.time_attendance.description: Review missing punches, schedule mismatches, time entries, and overtime
app.time_attendance.header_description: Compare actual clocks with the rostered shift before they reach payroll — scoped to one legal entity.
app.time_attendance.empty_overview: Select a legal entity to load its attendance trend.
app.time_attendance.empty_entries: Select a legal entity to review its time entries.
app.time_attendance.attendance_readiness: A CLOSED entry with both stamps can be measured into payroll. State only describes the clock. Overtime authorised is the separate day-level decision that lets a clock overrun reach payroll; the platform approval stamp governs edits to the whole attendance row.
app.time_attendance.chart_description: Open or incomplete punches as a share of recorded attendance over the latest eight weeks.
app.time_attendance.import_pipeline_desc: Import clock punches from the time-entries template — one row per person per day on its "Time entries" sheet, read as local wall time in the zone its "Settings" sheet names.

component.not_yet_due: Not yet due. The {period} payroll run deducts this instalment.
component.awaiting_run_title: No payroll run exists for {period} yet. This instalment is deducted when that run is built.
component.awaiting_rebuild_title: The {period} payroll run is still a draft, so nothing has been deducted yet. Recalculating that run takes this instalment.
component.missed_paid_title: The {period} payroll run was paid without this instalment, so the money was never recovered. A paid run is never rebuilt — reschedule the outstanding amount into a period that is still open.

component.no_refresh: Payroll updated, but the detail did not refresh.

component.lock_warning: Locking marks this payroll paid and makes its snapshot and payslips immutable. Select "Confirm lock & pay" to continue.
component.payslips_description: Open a payslip for its direct component and statutory line breakdown.
component.component_breakdown_descriptio: Each row is the direct, queryable link from this payslip to its pay component, input entry, or statutory scheme.
component.employments_description: One row per company this person works for. hire_date drives service months and every leave accrual.
component.contractual_terms_description: Effective-dated pay and classification for each engagement. End-date and insert a successor; never update in place.
component.statutory_registrations_descri: Where each engagement stands with each statutory scheme — registered with a reference, or not registered with a reason.
component.statutory_contributions_descri: The schemes this regime levies, in the order payroll applies them. Open one for the rate bands that price it — a band belongs to a scheme, not to the jurisdiction.
component.overtime_rules_description: What an hour beyond normal is worth here: one band of hours (or fractions of a normal day) on one kind of day, and the multiple it pays.
component.overtime_limits_description: The statutory ceilings per day, week or month. Read the unit: a limit either counts overtime hours or every hour worked, and the two are not interchangeable. Exceeding any of them stops a run, whatever on_exceed says.
component.overtime_coverage_description: Who the overtime ladder applies to here: the wage ceiling that ends coverage, the wage figure it is measured against, and the work categories covered or excluded whatever the wage. No rule means everyone is covered.
component.rest_and_meal_breaks_descripti: The statutory break: how many consecutive hours trigger it, how long it must run, and whether it counts as working time. A blank pay column means the authority does not settle it.
component.ordinary_pay_note: Ordinary pay is divided by {divisor} {unit} a month. Every rule here is effective-dated — end-date and insert a successor, never update in place.
component.rate_bands_description: One rung of this scheme's ladder: the selector that picks it — wage, wage and age, headcount or risk class — and the award it pays. A floor is the first band, a ceiling the terminal one.
component.create_run_hint: Creating the run builds it: the payslips and their complete component lines are written before this closes.
component.provision_remainder_hint: The remainder, if any, is placed on the final instalment so the total is exact.
component.risk_class_hint: The occupational risk group the entity is rated in, where its regime prices a contribution by risk. Indonesia's JKK is the one such scheme here: class {class_iv} is charged at 0.89% and class {class_i} at 0.24%, so an Indonesian entity left blank matches no band and its payroll run stops by name rather than quietly charging nothing. Malaysian and Philippine entities have no risk-keyed contribution and correctly leave this empty.
component.definition_overtime_excess: Overtime excess · {day} · {measure} from {from} · after {hours} total work hours
component.band_beyond_normal: Beyond normal hours: {from} h to {to} h
